title: Amazon Linux 2 2017.12 - ALAS2-2026-4133: medium priority package update for ImageMagick
description:
Package updates are available for Amazon Linux 2 that fix the following vulnerabilities:
CVE-2026-93588:
	ImageMagick before 7.1.2-31 and before 6.9.13-56 contains a NULL pointer dereference in the PNM coder. When the coder reaches a memory (resource) limit at a specific point during processing, the failed allocation is not handled and a NULL pointer is dereferenced, which can lead to a denial of service (application crash) when processing a specially crafted or sufficiently large PNM image.

CVE-2026-93587:
	ImageMagick before 7.1.2-31 and before 6.9.13-56 contains a policy bypass in the PCD (and, per the upstream advisory, CUBE and HALD) coder: when a specific command line option is supplied, the decoder does not check a configured resource limit, which can result in extra memory allocation. A local user able to pass command line options to ImageMagick can therefore exceed the intended memory policy limit, causing a limited availability impact. The issue is fixed in 7.1.2-31 and 6.9.13-56.

CVE-2026-93586:
	ImageMagick before 7.1.2-31 and before 6.9.13-56 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the ImagesToBlob method, caused by a pointer that is not updated correctly. Exploitation may result in a limited availability impact (e.g., a crash of the affected process). The issue is fixed in versions 7.1.2-31 and 6.9.13-56.

CVE-2026-123273:
	ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 and 6.9.13-60 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in the SVG decoder because QueueAuthenticPixelCacheNexus in MagickCore/cache.c fails to validate requested region width and height. Attackers can supply a crafted SVG image that repeatedly requests a non-advancing pixel region, consuming CPU and hanging the decoding worker.

CVE-2026-116160:
	A flaw was found in ImageMagick. An attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by tricking a user into processing a specially crafted image file using the X11 animate feature. Processing the image triggers a heap-based buffer overflow, writing data beyond allocated memory limits, which corrupts memory and crashes the application.

CVE-2026-116159:
	A flaw was found in ImageMagick. The handling of the color decision list (-cdl) option fails to properly release allocated memory after use. An attacker can exploit this issue by providing input that repeatedly processes the -cdl option, leading to excessive memory consumption and a Denial of Service (DoS) through resource exhaustion.

CVE-2026-116157:
	A flaw was found in ImageMagick. The PerlMagick component fails to properly release memory allocated when reading image properties. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by repeatedly triggering property read operations to exhaust system memory, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).

CVE-2026-116156:
	ImageMagick before 6.9.13-58 and 7.x before 7.1.2-33 contains a memory leak caused by a missing cleanup when the -set profile option is used. An attacker who induces a user to process images with the -set profile option can leak memory, potentially exhausting resources and causing a denial of service.

CVE-2026-116155:
	A flaw was found in ImageMagick. A remote attacker could cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by supplying an image with a specially crafted Extensible Metadata Platform (XMP) profile. When affected decoders process the malformed profile, memory is repeatedly leaked, which can eventually lead to system resource exhaustion.

CVE-2026-116154:
	A flaw was found in ImageMagick. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by submitting specially crafted, deeply nested XML data. When processing the input, the application fails to release allocated memory upon reaching the nesting depth limit, resulting in memory exhaustion.

CVE-2026-116151:
	A flaw was found in ImageMagick. A remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by supplying a specially crafted image file to be encoded into the JPEG Network Graphics (JNG) format. Due to a failure to properly release allocated memory in the JNG encoder, processing these files can lead to memory exhaustion and service instability.

CVE-2026-116148:
	A flaw was found in ImageMagick. The Magick Vector Graphics (MVG) encoder does not properly neutralize user-specified drawing options before writing them into generated output. An attacker capable of supplying drawing options can exploit this vulnerability to inject arbitrary drawing commands into the resulting MVG file, potentially leading to unauthorized information disclosure.

CVE-2026-116146:
	A flaw was found in ImageMagick. The Magick Scripting Language (MSL) decoder fails to release allocated memory when processing specially crafted MSL files. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing malicious MSL files for processing, resulting in excessive resource consumption and a Denial of Service (DoS).

CVE-2026-116145:
	ImageMagick before 6.9.13-58 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 contains a security policy bypass caused by an incomplete fix for the policy bypass reported in GHSA-jjp4-3fwf-393j. An attacker able to supply input to ImageMagick can evade configured security policy restrictions, allowing operations the policy was intended to block.

CVE-2026-116144:
	A flaw was found in ImageMagick. An attacker could cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by supplying a specially crafted Magick Vector Graphics (MVG) file. When processed, the file triggers uncontrolled recursion within the MVG decoder, exhausting stack memory and causing the application to crash.

CVE-2026-116143:
	A flaw was found in ImageMagick. This vulnerability allows a local attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) through resource exhaustion. The PostScript (PS), Portable Document Format (PDF), and XML Paper Specification (XPS) decoders fail to properly enforce security policy list length limits on scene selection, allowing an attacker supplying specific arguments to trigger excessive processing.

CVE-2026-116140:
	A flaw was found in ImageMagick. An attacker could bypass administrator-defined security policies by convincing the application to process specially crafted input that triggers a delegate invocation. This issue occurs due to incorrect parsing of delegate commands, allowing programs explicitly restricted or blocked in the security configuration to be executed.

CVE-2026-109964:
	ImageMagick before 7.1.2-33 and 6.9.13-58 contains a heap buffer underwrite vulnerability in DecodeImage() in coders/pict.c on 32-bit builds due to pointer arithmetic overflow. Attackers can supply a crafted PICT file with maximized row, column and bytes-per-line values to bypass bounds checks and write up to 128 controlled bytes below the heap buffer, causing crashes or code execution.

CVE-2026-109282:
	ImageMagick before 6.9.13-57 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 contains a type confusion flaw in the INFO, JSON and YAML encoders, where an internal method receives a pointer of an unexpected type when writing an image in a compressed format. An attacker who can cause such an image write can trigger a SIGABRT or SIGSEGV, crashing the process and causing denial of service.

CVE-2026-109279:
	ImageMagick before 6.9.13-57 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 lacks proper synchronization when the security policy is accessed, so simultaneous reads and writes of the policy by multiple threads trigger a race condition that causes a heap buffer over-write. An attacker able to induce concurrent security policy access can crash the application, causing a denial of service.

CVE-2026-109278:
	ImageMagick before 6.9.13-57 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 contains a memory leak in the wavelet-denoise operation, which fails to release allocated memory when a required resource cannot be acquired. Attackers can repeatedly trigger wavelet-denoise processing under resource-constrained conditions to leak memory and degrade service availability.

CVE-2026-109277:
	ImageMagick before 7.1.2-32 contains a policy bypass vulnerability in the -script operation due to missing checks on file descriptor handling. Attackers can use the -script operation to close file descriptors not opened by the current operation, circumventing configured security policies.

CVE-2026-109276:
	ImageMagick before 6.9.13-57 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 contains an incomplete cleanup flaw in the JNG decoder that fails to remove temporary files when processing crafted input. Attackers can submit crafted JNG files for processing to repeatedly leak temporary files, consuming disk space and degrading availability.

CVE-2026-109275:
	ImageMagick before 6.9.13-57 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 contains a code injection vulnerability in the MVG decoder when a PostScript renderer is used. Attackers can supply a crafted MVG file that, when decoded, injects code into the PostScript rendering path.

CVE-2026-109273:
	ImageMagick before 6.9.13-57 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the PostScript decoder, which allocates a buffer one byte longer than the data it decoded. Attackers can supply a crafted PostScript file to expose a single uninitialized byte of memory contents.

CVE-2026-109270:
	ImageMagick before 7.1.2-32 contains a memory leak vulnerability in the -process option that allows attackers to cause unreleased memory allocations by supplying certain arguments. Attackers can repeatedly invoke the -process option with crafted arguments to gradually exhaust memory and degrade service availability.

CVE-2026-109269:
	ImageMagick before 6.9.13-57 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the JPEG decoder, which performs a read that exposes uninitialized memory when handling crafted input. Attackers can supply a crafted JPEG file for processing to disclose uninitialized memory contents.

CVE-2026-109266:
	ImageMagick before 6.9.13-57 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 contains an XML injection vulnerability in the CIP encoder, which does not properly escape input-derived data when writing Cisco IP Phone XML output. Attackers can supply a crafted file that, when converted to CIP format, injects arbitrary markup into the generated XML.

CVE-2026-109264:
	ImageMagick before 6.9.13-57 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 contains uncontrolled recursion in the MVG decoder that can exhaust the program stack. An attacker who controls a file name processed by ImageMagick can trigger a stack overflow that crashes the process, causing a denial of service.

CVE-2026-109263:
	ImageMagick before 6.9.13-57 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 contains a memory leak in the YUV encoder, which fails to release allocated memory when a specific operation fails. Attackers can supply crafted input that triggers the failing encoder operation, leaking memory and potentially exhausting resources to cause a denial of service.

CVE-2026-109262:
	ImageMagick before 6.9.13-57 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 contains a memory leak in the SVG encoder (WriteSVGImage) that fails to release allocated memory when handling crafted images. Attackers can supply crafted image files that are processed by the SVG encoder to leak memory and cause a denial of service through resource consumption.

CVE-2026-109261:
	ImageMagick before 6.9.13-57 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 contains a memory leak in the GIF encoder because allocated memory is not released when color quantization fails during encoding. Attackers can supply images whose GIF conversion causes quantization to fail, leaking memory with each attempt and degrading availability.

CVE-2026-107210:
	ImageMagick is free and open-source software used for editing and manipulating digital images. Prior to 7.1.2-30 and 6.9.13-55, a crafted highly compressed MAT image can make the MAT decoder create temporary files larger than the configured security-policy limit, bypassing resource restrictions and consuming excessive disk space. This issue is fixed in versions 7.1.2-30 and 6.9.13-55.

CVE-2026-107208:
	ImageMagick is free and open-source software used for editing and manipulating digital images. Prior to 7.1.2-30 and 6.9.13-55, a crafted XMP profile can reach a recursion limit that is handled as a fatal condition instead of an ordinary exception, terminating the image-processing process. This issue is fixed in versions 7.1.2-30 and 6.9.13-55.

CVE-2026-106580:
	ImageMagick is free and open-source software used for editing and manipulating digital images. Prior to 7.1.2-31 and 6.9.13-56, a missing security-policy check in the CUT encoder allows a crafted local encoding operation to read data that policy should deny and can also cause a crash. This issue is fixed in versions 7.1.2-31 and 6.9.13-56.

CVE-2026-106579:
	ImageMagick is free and open-source software used for editing and manipulating digital images. Prior to 7.1.2-31 and 6.9.13-56, a crafted image can bypass an ImageMagick security policy that uses coder as its domain, potentially allowing data prohibited by the policy to be read. This issue is fixed in versions 7.1.2-31 and 6.9.13-56.

CVE-2026-106578:
	ImageMagick is free and open-source software used for editing and manipulating digital images. Prior to 7.1.2-31 and 6.9.13-56, a crafted image can cause an invalid memory free in the MVG decoder and crash the process. This issue is fixed in versions 7.1.2-31 and 6.9.13-56.

CVE-2026-106577:
	ImageMagick is free and open-source software used for editing and manipulating digital images. Prior to 7.1.2-31 and 6.9.13-56, unescaped or untrimmed values can inject code into output generated by PostScript coders. This issue is fixed in versions 7.1.2-31 and 6.9.13-56.

CVE-2026-106573:
	ImageMagick is free and open-source software used for editing and manipulating digital images. Prior to 7.1.2-31 and 6.9.13-56, a missing limit check in the MVG decoder allows a crafted MVG image to trigger an excessively long-running operation. This issue is fixed in versions 7.1.2-31 and 6.9.13-56.

CVE-2026-106572:
	ImageMagick is free and open-source software used for editing and manipulating digital images. Prior to 7.1.2-30 and 6.9.13-55, a missing recursion-depth check in the CALS decoder allows a crafted CALS image to exhaust the call stack and terminate the process. This issue is fixed in versions 7.1.2-30 and 6.9.13-55.

CVE-2026-106571:
	ImageMagick is free and open-source software used for editing and manipulating digital images. Prior to 6.9.13-56 and 7.1.2-31, a crafted local call to the GetVirtualPixels API can trigger an integer calculation error and write beyond a heap buffer, crashing the server process. This issue is fixed in versions 6.9.13-56 and 7.1.2-31.

CVE-2026-106570:
	ImageMagick is free and open-source software used for editing and manipulating digital images. Prior to 7.1.2-32, an unauthenticated adjacent-network client can repeatedly connect to the distributed pixel cache server and exhaust its available connections, causing denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 7.1.2-32.

CVE-2026-106568:
	ImageMagick is free and open-source software used for editing and manipulating digital images. Prior to 7.1.2-32 and 6.9.13-57, a crafted XMP profile embedded in an image can cause the profile parser to enter an infinite loop, preventing image processing from completing. This issue is fixed in versions 7.1.2-32 and 6.9.13-57.

CVE-2026-106566:
	ImageMagick is free and open-source software used for editing and manipulating digital images. Prior to 7.1.2-32, delegate symlink cleanup does not check the MAGICK_SHRED_PASSES environment variable, allowing a local privileged workflow to overwrite a file with random data. This issue is fixed in version 7.1.2-32.

CVE-2026-106565:
	ImageMagick is free and open-source software used for editing and manipulating digital images. Prior to 7.1.2-32 and 6.9.13-57, a missing end-of-file check while reading bzip2-compressed image data can cause an infinite loop and exhaust processing resources. This issue is fixed in versions 7.1.2-32 and 6.9.13-57.

CVE-2026-105827:
	ImageMagick before 7.1.2-30 and 6.9.13-55 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in the CALS decoder due to a missing depth check. Attackers can supply a crafted CALS image that triggers unbounded recursion, exhausting the stack and crashing the process, resulting in a denial of service.

CVE-2026-105826:
	ImageMagick before 6.9.13-55 and 7.x before 7.1.2-30 contains a security policy bypass in the MAT decoder, which does not enforce configured temporary file size limits when reading highly compressed data. Attackers can supply a crafted MAT image whose decompressed data is written to temporary files larger than the policy allows, consuming disk resources.

CVE-2026-105825:
	ImageMagick before 6.9.13-55 and 7.x before 7.1.2-30 contains a denial of service vulnerability in its handling of XMP profiles, where a crafted profile terminates the process instead of raising an exception. Attackers can supply images with malicious XMP profiles to crash applications that process them using ImageMagick.

CVE-2026-105823:
	ImageMagick before 6.9.13-56 and 7.x before 7.1.2-31 lacks a security policy check in the CUT encoder, allowing configured security policies to be bypassed. Attackers can supply crafted input processed by the CUT encoder to crash the application or leak sensitive data.

CVE-2026-105405:
	ImageMagick before 6.9.13-56 and 7.x before 7.1.2-31 contains an invalid memory free vulnerability in the MVG decoder. Attackers can supply a crafted MVG image for processing to trigger the invalid free and crash the application, causing a denial of service.

CVE-2026-105404:
	ImageMagick before 6.9.13-56 and 7.x before 7.1.2-31 contains a code injection vulnerability in its PostScript coders, because some values are not properly escaped or trimmed when written to output. Attackers can supply crafted values that embed arbitrary PostScript code into files generated by these coders.

CVE-2026-105403:
	ImageMagick before 6.9.13-56 and 7.x before 7.1.2-31 allows a security policy bypass when a policy uses coder, rather than module, as its domain. An attacker can supply a crafted image to evade coder-based policy restrictions, causing ImageMagick to process formats the administrator intended to block.

CVE-2026-105399:
	ImageMagick before 6.9.13-56 and 7.x before 7.1.2-31 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the MVG decoder caused by a missing limit check. Attackers can supply a crafted MVG image that triggers a long-running decoding operation, consuming excessive CPU resources and stalling image processing.

CVE-2026-105398:
	ImageMagick before 7.1.2-31 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability that allows attackers to overwrite heap memory by making a crafted call to the GetVirtualPixels API. Attackers can trigger the out-of-bounds heap write through crafted input to crash the server, causing a denial of service.

CVE-2026-105083:
	A flaw was found in ImageMagick. A local attacker with permission to modify the security policy configuration file can bypass defined security restrictions by supplying an alternate XML document type declaration (DOCTYPE). Due to improper parsing of certain DOCTYPE declarations, the configuration parser consumes the remainder of the file and silently fails to load security rules. As a result, restricted or forbidden operations are permitted to execute.

CVE-2026-105081:
	ImageMagick before 6.9.13-58 and 7.x before 7.1.2-33 does not properly account for symbolic links in the IsRightsAuthorizedByName security policy check, allowing configured policy restrictions to be bypassed. Local attackers who can create a symlink can point it at a policy-restricted path to evade the configured policy.

CVE-2026-102635:
	ImageMagick versions before 7.1.2-32 and 6.9.13-57 contain uninitialized heap memory disclosure in the GIF decoder's application extension handler in coders/gif.c. Attackers can craft malicious GIF files that cause the number parser to read uninitialized heap memory and store contents as image metadata, disclosing sensitive heap information.
